localBiteReport: The most current inshore report for Choctawhatchee Bay comes from the week of October 23–29, 2026. According to Capt. Blake Nelson of Last Cast Charters (via Great Days Outdoors), the redfish bite on the bay's flats has held up well despite a recent hurricane — the bay took on a tannin-stained appearance rather than heavy mud, and sight fishing has remained productive in the Destin area. Smaller slot-sized reds (roughly 23 inches and under) are still working familiar guts, potholes, and shallow feeding areas, while larger upper-slot and overslot fish are beginning to shift into a more mobile fall pattern. A separate charter guide report on captainexperiences.com (from approximately two weeks prior) also noted redfish and trout active in the bayous. Flounder are not specifically called out in this week's report, but Half Hitch's longstanding October forecast notes that flounder begin their fall bay migration in early October, staging in the harbor and around docks before heading offshore — so they should be worth targeting now. Water temperature at this location is 75°F.
